content:
Yesterday's Mac Studio launch with the M5 Max chip brought a pleasant surprise: the starting price remains at $2,499, unchanged from the M4 Max Mac Studio.

However, if you're looking to upgrade the GPU, watch out for a hidden cost—$300 more than the price initially shown on Apple's website...

This hidden upgrade fee caught John Gruber off guard while he was sorting through the pricing for each configuration of yesterday's newly announced machines.

The base configuration features an 18-core CPU paired with a 32-core GPU. Apple's website lists an upgrade to a 40-core GPU, clearly showing an additional $300 charge.

The catch is that selecting this option also bumps the memory from 32GB to 48GB, costing another $300. Since there's no way to upgrade just the GPU cores without also upgrading to 48GB of memory, the actual upgrade cost is double what's listed—$600.

When you select the chip upgrade, Apple uses somewhat vague language to alert you to this.

Are you tempted to buy the new Mac Mini or Mac Studio? Share your thoughts in the comments.
